 - Edit files: Use Edit (NOT sed/awk)

 - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes in your command (e.g., cd "path with spaces/file.txt")
 - Try to maintain your current working directory throughout the session by using absolute paths and avoiding usage of `cd`. You may use `cd` if the User explicitly requests it. In particular, never prepend `cd <current-directory>` to a `git` command — `git` already operates on the current working tree, and the compound triggers a permission prompt.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

1	---
2	title: Issue service detailed design
3	id: DES-ISSUE
4	status: approved
5	owners: [m.lindqvist]
6	last_updated: 2026-05-22
7	related: [REQ-060, REQ-061, REQ-062, REQ-066, ADR-003, ADR-013]
8	---
9	
10	## Purpose
11	
12	`src/server/services/issue-service.ts` owns everything that turns a create/update/status
13	request into a row in the `issues` table plus the events every reactive concern in Taskflow
14	hangs off: notifications (DES-121 .. DES-127), search indexing (DES-154 .. DES-158), the
15	audit log (DES-170 .. DES-174), webhook fan-out (DES-159 .. DES-163) and the usage counters
16	(DES-135 .. DES-141). It is the largest service in the layer by function count because an
17	issue is the object almost everything else in the product reacts to.
18	
19	What it deliberately does not own: numbering scheme storage (delegated to
20	`src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts`'s `nextIssueNumber`), label assignment (owned
21	by `src/server/services/label-service.ts`), attachment quota accounting (owned by
22	`src/server/services/attachment-service.ts`), and comment threading (owned by
23	`src/server/services/comment-service.ts`). Board rendering order is explicitly
24	presentation-only — DES-104 covers why `moveIssue` does not persist a position column.
25	
26	Every exported function follows the same shape and it is worth stating once instead of
27	per-function: `assertOrgScope` first, then a `requireFound` load of the row (or its parent,
28	for `createIssue`), then `assertCan` against a `PermissionResource` built by one of the
29	`_support.ts` helpers, then `assertNotArchived` where archiving matters, then the write, then
30	`emit`. DES-100 names this order explicitly because two tests
31	(`tests/services/issue-service.test.ts`, `tests/services/issue-service.scope.test.ts`) assert
32	on it directly by checking which error surfaces when two guards would both fail.
33	
34	## Public surface
35	
36	| function | signature | permission action | events emitted | errors thrown |
37	|---|---|---|---|---|
38	| `createIssue` | `(actor: Actor, input: CreateIssueInput) => Promise<Issue>` | `issue:create` | `issue.created` | `NotFoundError`, `PermissionDeniedError`, `AlreadyArchivedError`, plain `Error` (quota) |
39	| `updateIssue` | `(actor: Actor, input: UpdateIssueInput) => Promise<Issue>` | `issue:update` | `issue.updated` | `NotFoundError`, `PermissionDeniedError`, `AlreadyArchivedError` |
40	| `changeIssueStatus` | `(actor: Actor, input: ChangeIssueStatusInput) => Promise<Issue>` | `issue:update` | `issue.status_changed` | `NotFoundError`, `PermissionDeniedError`, `AlreadyArchivedError` |
41	| `assignIssue` | `(actor: Actor, input: AssignIssueInput) => Promise<Issue>` | `issue:assign` | `issue.assigned` or `issue.updated` | `NotFoundError`, `PermissionDeniedError`, `AlreadyArchivedError` |
42	| `archiveIssue` | `(actor: Actor, orgId: OrgId, issueId: IssueId) => Promise<Issue>` | `issue:archive` | `issue.archived` | `NotFoundError`, `PermissionDeniedError`, `AlreadyArchivedError` |
43	| `moveIssue` | `(actor: Actor, input: MoveIssueInput) => Promise<Issue>` | `issue:update` (delegated) | `issue.status_changed` | same as `changeIssueStatus` |
44	| `getIssue` | `(actor: Actor, orgId: OrgId, issueId: IssueId) => Promise<IssueWithRelations>` | `issue:read` | none | `NotFoundError`, `PermissionDeniedError` |
45	| `listIssues` | `(actor: Actor, input: IssueFilterInput) => Promise<Page<Issue>>` | `issue:read` | none | `PermissionDeniedError` |
46	| `getBoard` | `(actor: Actor, orgId: OrgId, projectId: ProjectId) => Promise<readonly IssueBoardColumn[]>` | `issue:read` | none | `NotFoundError`, `PermissionDeniedError` |
47	
48	## Collaborators
49	
50	- `src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts` — `countIssues`, `nextIssueNumber`,
51	  `insertIssue`, `findIssueById`, `updateIssue`, `setIssueStatus`, `setIssueAssignee`,
52	  `archiveIssue`, `listIssues`, `listBoardColumns`.
53	- `src/server/repositories/project-repository.ts` — `findProjectById`, used to load the
54	  parent for `createIssue` and `getBoard`.
55	- `src/server/repositories/organization-repository.ts` — `findOrgById`, the source of the
56	  plan used in the quota check.
57	- `src/server/repositories/label-repository.ts` — `listLabelsForIssues`, called from
58	  `getIssue` to hydrate `IssueWithRelations`.
59	- `src/server/repositories/comment-repository.ts` and
60	  `src/server/repositories/attachment-repository.ts` — counts folded into `getIssue`'s
61	  response.
62	- `src/config/plan-limits.ts` — `wouldExceedLimit`, the quota gate in `createIssue`.
63	- `src/lib/permissions.ts` — `assertCan`; `src/lib/tenant.ts` — `assertOrgScope`;
64	  `src/lib/soft-delete.ts` — `assertNotArchived`; `src/lib/event-bus.ts` — `emit`.
65	- `src/server/services/_support.ts` — `actorEnvelope`, `issueResource`, `orgResource`,
66	  `projectResource`, `requireFound`, all reused verbatim rather than reimplemented per
67	  function, per ADR-003 and ADR-013.
68	
69	### DES-100 — Every mutating method runs guards in the same fixed order
70	
71	- **Satisfies:** REQ-011, REQ-021, REQ-071
72	- **Decided in:** ADR-003, ADR-013
73	- **Code:** `src/server/services/issue-service.ts` — `createIssue`, `updateIssue`,
74	  `changeIssueStatus`, `assignIssue`, `archiveIssue`
75	
76	Every mutating function in this file runs `assertOrgScope(actor, input.orgId)` before it
77	touches a repository, then loads the row with `requireFound`, then calls `assertCan` with a
78	resource built from the *loaded* row rather than from the caller's input, then (where the
79	entity supports archiving) calls `assertNotArchived`. The order is not incidental: tenant
80	scope is the cheapest check and fails closed before any row from another organization is
81	even read, matching the cross-tenant guard's priority in the `can()` decision order described
82	in ADR-003. Building the `PermissionResource` from the *stored* row rather than trusting the
83	request body is what makes ownership escalation (`issue:update`, `issue:archive`) correct —
84	`issueResource(before)` carries the real `authorId` and `assigneeId`, which is what lets
85	`can()` grant `granted_by_ownership` to an author editing their own issue even at `viewer`
86	rank, per REQ-072. Reversing the archived check and the permission check would leak whether
87	an issue exists to a caller who cannot read it at all; reversing scope and everything else
88	would let a cross-tenant `issueId` reach a repository call. The consistency across all five
89	mutating functions is deliberate enough that `tests/services/issue-service.scope.test.ts`
90	runs the same table of cases against every one of them.
91	
92	### DES-101 — Issue creation gates on four things before a number is allocated
93	
94	- **Satisfies:** REQ-060, REQ-061, REQ-064, REQ-065
95	- **Decided in:** ADR-003, ADR-010
96	- **Code:** `src/server/services/issue-service.ts` — `createIssue`
97	
98	`createIssue` checks, strictly in order: tenant scope, that the parent project exists and is
99	not archived (`assertNotArchived("Project", ...)`), the `issue:create` permission evaluated
100	against that project (not the org — REQ-060 makes a project the sole scope of issue
101	existence), and finally the per-project issue quota via `wouldExceedLimit(org.plan,
102	"issuesPerProject", used)`, where `used` comes from `issueRepo.countIssues`. Only after all
103	four gates pass does the function call `issueRepo.nextIssueNumber(input.orgId,
104	input.projectId)`, which is the per-project counter behind REQ-061's "allocated per project
105	and never reused" guarantee — the repository never reuses a number even if the issue that
106	held it is later archived, because the counter is monotonic and stored independently of the
107	`issues` table's row count. Ordering the quota check after the permission check, rather than
108	before, means a caller who cannot create issues at all gets a `PermissionDeniedError` rather
109	than a confusing quota message; ordering it before allocation means a rejected request never
110	consumes a number, which would otherwise create visible gaps in the sequence a customer might
111	reasonably ask support about. The created issue is returned with `issue.created` published
112	carrying `assigneeId` and `priority` in the payload — REQ-065 is satisfied by this single
113	`emit` call, and every listener (notification fan-out, activity log, search index, usage
114	counters, webhook bridge) reads the same event rather than re-querying the row.
115	
116	### DES-102 — updateIssue reports exactly the fields the caller changed
117	
118	- **Satisfies:** REQ-068
119	- **Decided in:** ADR-005
120	- **Code:** `src/server/services/issue-service.ts` — `updateIssue`
121	
122	`updateIssue` computes `changedFields` as `Object.keys(input).filter((key) => key !== "orgId"
123	&& key !== "issueId")` — every remaining key in the validated `UpdateIssueInput` is reported,
124	which is a coarser signal than "fields that actually differ from the stored value" (that
125	finer computation exists as `changedFields()` in `_support.ts` and is used elsewhere, notably
126	by services that diff `before`/`after` pairs, but `issue-service.ts` does not call it here).
127	The practical effect for REQ-068 is that a caller who resubmits an unchanged field is still
128	reported as having changed it; this is a known simplification the team accepted because Zod
129	validation on `UpdateIssueInput` already makes every field optional, so most callers only
130	submit fields they intend to change, and the alternative (loading the pre-image and diffing)
131	would double a already-common write path's repository round-trips for a case the UI does not
132	produce. The emitted `issue.updated` payload never carries the new values themselves, only
133	the list of changed field names — listeners that need the value re-read the row, which is the
134	same "trust the row, not the payload" discipline DES-158 documents for the search indexer.
135	
136	### DES-103 — Status transitions are validated against the closed status union and are idempotent no-ops when unchanged
137	
138	- **Satisfies:** REQ-062, REQ-066
139	- **Decided in:** ADR-003, ADR-009
140	- **Code:** `src/server/services/issue-service.ts` — `changeIssueStatus`
141	
142	The status a caller may set is constrained at the schema boundary: `ChangeIssueStatusInput`
143	is a Zod schema (ADR-009's shared-schema pattern) whose `status` field is the same closed
144	union `issueRepo.setIssueStatus` accepts, so `changeIssueStatus` itself performs no further
145	validation of the value — REQ-062's "closed vocabulary" is enforced once, at the type
146	boundary, not re-checked in the service. What the service does own is the transition: after
147	the standard guard sequence (DES-100), it compares `before.status === input.status` and
148	returns the unchanged row immediately if so, without writing to the repository and without
149	emitting `issue.status_changed`. This makes the endpoint safe to call from an optimistic UI
150	that might redundantly resubmit the current status (REQ-062, ADR-021's optimistic-update
151	pattern) without generating a spurious event that would otherwise show up twice in the
152	activity feed and trigger a webhook delivery for a transition that never happened. When the
153	status genuinely changes, the emitted payload carries both `from` and `before.status` and
154	`to: after.status`, which is what lets `src/server/services/activity-service.ts`'s
155	`registerActivityListeners` render "Status open → in_progress" without a second read. Status
156	changes use the same `issue:update` permission as any other field edit — there is no
157	dedicated `issue:transition` action in `ROLE_MATRIX` — which means the role matrix cannot
158	express "may reassign but not re-open," a limitation the team accepted rather than growing
159	the permission surface for a distinction the product has never asked for.
160	
161	### DES-104 — Board drag-and-drop is a status change plus a touch, not a persisted order
162	
163	- **Satisfies:** REQ-066, REQ-077
164	- **Decided in:** ADR-021
165	- **Code:** `src/server/services/issue-service.ts` — `moveIssue`, `getBoard`
166	
167	`moveIssue` is a thin wrapper: it takes a `MoveIssueInput` (`orgId`, `issueId`, `toStatus`)
168	and calls `changeIssueStatus(actor, { orgId, issueId, status: input.toStatus })` directly,
169	inheriting every guard and event from DES-103 rather than duplicating them. The code comment
170	in the source is explicit about why there is no persisted card index: "the index is
171	presentation-only — the board renders by `updated_at`." That means two clients dragging cards
172	in the same column concurrently do not fight over an integer position column; the board's
173	sort order is a side effect of `changeIssueStatus`'s write, which always touches `updated_at`.

175	status column, without changing status, produces no repository write and no visible reorder
176	after a refresh — the UI only persists cross-column moves. `getBoard` is a pure read: it loads
177	the project, asserts `issue:read` against it, and defers entirely to
178	`issueRepo.listBoardColumns`, which does the status-bucketing server-side so the client never
179	computes columns from a flat issue list.
180	
181	### DES-105 — Assignment is a separate permission from update, and un-assigning degrades to issue.updated
182	
183	- **Satisfies:** REQ-067
184	- **Decided in:** ADR-003, ADR-005
185	- **Code:** `src/server/services/issue-service.ts` — `assignIssue`
186	
187	`assignIssue` checks `issue:assign`, a permission distinct from `issue:update` in
188	`ROLE_MATRIX` (both require `member` minimum, but they are separate matrix entries so a
189	future role split does not have to touch this call site). The reason assignment has its own

192	workflow that should not require `issue:update` rights over content the reassigner did not
193	author. The function branches on `input.assigneeId === null`: unassigning publishes
194	`issue.updated` with `changedFields: ["assigneeId"]` rather than `issue.assigned`, because
195	`issue.assigned`'s payload contract requires a non-null `assigneeId` — `TaskflowEventMap`
196	types the field as `UserId`, not `UserId | null`, so a null assignment literally cannot be
197	represented in that event shape. Assigning to a real user publishes `issue.assigned` carrying

199	`notification-service.ts`'s `issue.assigned` handler notify only the new assignee (DES-122)
200	without a second lookup, and what lets the activity log render "Assigned to X" without
201	needing the prior value.

203	### DES-106 — getIssue composes three repositories into one read model, and never authorizes the composed pieces separately
204	
205	- **Satisfies:** REQ-074, REQ-075, REQ-077
206	- **Decided in:** ADR-013
207	- **Code:** `src/server/services/issue-service.ts` — `getIssue`
208	
209	`getIssue` authorizes once, against `issue:read` on the loaded issue, and then freely composes
210	three additional repository reads without further permission checks: `labelRepo
211	.listLabelsForIssues` (REQ-074, org-shared labels), `commentRepo.countComments`, and
212	`attachmentRepo.listAttachments(...).length` (REQ-075, storage-quota-tracked attachments).
213	This is a deliberate reading of ADR-013's "services own authorization, repositories own
214	tenancy" boundary: once a caller has proven they may read the issue, its label assignments,
215	comment count, and attachment count are treated as part of the same resource rather than as
216	independently protected sub-resources, because none of them can be read meaningfully on their
217	own — a label list without knowing which issue it decorates, or a comment count without the
218	issue it counts, has no product surface. This is narrower than `comment-service.ts`'s
219	`getThread`, which re-checks `comment:read` even though it also starts from a loaded issue —
220	the two services made different calls about whether the sub-resource has its own reachable
221	endpoint (comments do, via `/issues/:id/comments`; label and attachment *counts* on the issue

224	### DES-107 — listIssues authorizes at the organization, not per project, because visibility narrows later
225	
226	- **Satisfies:** REQ-050, REQ-077, REQ-078
227	- **Decided in:** ADR-008

231	individual project, with an explicit comment marking the trade-off: "a cross-project list is
232	an org-wide read; per-project visibility is enforced when the caller opens an individual
233	issue." That means a viewer with org-wide `issue:read` can see issue titles and statuses from

235	permission wall if they try to open one. The team accepted this because private projects

238	and would make `IssueFilterInput`'s cursor semantics depend on membership state that can

243	## Sequence: creating an issue and its downstream fan-out
244	
245	```mermaid
246	sequenceDiagram
247	    participant UI as Issue create form
248	    participant Action as Server Action
249	    participant Svc as issue-service.createIssue
250	    participant Repo as issue-repository
251	    participant Bus as event-bus.emit
252	    participant Notif as notification-service
253	    participant Search as search-service
254	    participant Activity as activity-service
255	
256	    UI->>Action: submit CreateIssueInput
257	    Action->>Svc: createIssue(actor, input)
258	    Svc->>Svc: assertOrgScope(actor, input.orgId)
259	    Svc->>Repo: findProjectById
260	    Repo-->>Svc: project
261	    Svc->>Svc: assertNotArchived(project)
262	    Svc->>Svc: assertCan(issue:create, projectResource)
263	    Svc->>Repo: countIssues(orgId, projectId)
264	    Repo-->>Svc: used
265	    Svc->>Svc: wouldExceedLimit(plan, "issuesPerProject", used)
266	    Svc->>Repo: nextIssueNumber
267	    Repo-->>Svc: number
268	    Svc->>Repo: insertIssue
269	    Repo-->>Svc: issue
270	    Svc->>Bus: emit("issue.created", payload)
271	    Bus-->>Notif: (no direct subscriber to issue.created)
272	    Bus-->>Search: subscribe handler re-reads row, indexIssue

278	1. The UI submits a validated `CreateIssueInput` to a Server Action, which forwards it
279	   unchanged to `createIssue(actor, input)`.
280	2. The service asserts tenant scope first, then loads the parent project and confirms it is
281	   not archived before checking `issue:create` against it — a caller who cannot even see the
282	   project never learns whether the quota has room.
283	3. `issueRepo.countIssues` returns the current count for the quota comparison; `createIssue`
284	   never inserts the row before this check succeeds.
285	4. `issueRepo.nextIssueNumber` is only called once every prior gate has passed, so a rejected
286	   request leaves no gap in the per-project numbering sequence.
287	5. `issueRepo.insertIssue` writes the row and returns the persisted `Issue`, including its
288	   generated id and number.
289	6. `emit("issue.created", ...)` publishes the event synchronously to every subscriber
290	   registered through `event-registry.ts`; note that, unlike `issue.assigned`, no
291	   notification handler subscribes to `issue.created` directly — issue creation notifies
292	   nobody by design, since there is no assignee or mentioned user yet.
293	7. The search listener (DES-158) re-reads the issue by id rather than trusting the payload
294	   and calls `indexIssue`; the activity listener (DES-172) writes an audit row from the
295	   payload directly, since activity intentionally trusts event payloads for its summary text.
296	8. Control returns to the Server Action once `emit` resolves — Taskflow's event bus is

299	
300	## Failure modes
301	
302	| thrown error | resulting error code | caller behaviour |
303	|---|---|---|
304	| `NotFoundError` (from `requireFound`) | `not_found` (404) | UI shows "issue/project not found"; Server Action surfaces a toast, no retry |
305	| `PermissionDeniedError` (from `assertCan`) | `forbidden` (403) | Server Action returns a form error; UI hides the action that produced it once role is known |
306	| `TenantScopeError` (from `assertOrgScope`) | `tenant_scope_violation` (403) | Treated as a programming error client-side; logged, session redirected to org switcher |
307	| `AlreadyArchivedError` (from `assertNotArchived`) | `conflict` (409) | UI prompts to restore the project/issue before retrying the write |
308	| plain `Error` (quota message in `createIssue`) | falls through to `internal_error` (500) unless mapped upstream | UI shows a generic failure; this is a known gap — quota breaches in `issue-service.ts` are not raised as a typed `plan_limit_exceeded` the way `billing-service.ts`'s `assertWithinLimit` does, so the client cannot distinguish a quota breach from a genuine server fault by error code alone |
309	
310	The quota-error inconsistency in the last row is real and worth flagging in review: unlike
311	`project-service.ts`'s `createProject` (same pattern) and `billing-service.ts`'s
312	`assertWithinLimit` (which emits `billing.limit_exceeded` and is designed to map to
313	`plan_limit_exceeded`), `createIssue` throws a bare `Error` with a human-readable message
314	rather than a typed domain error. `src/lib/errors.ts`'s `HTTP_STATUS_BY_CODE` has no entry a
315	bare `Error` maps to other than the `internal_error` default, so a caller cannot render a
316	"upgrade your plan" call to action from the error alone today; the UI currently pattern
317	matches on the message string, which is fragile and flagged as a follow-up in the DES-135
318	billing design.
319	
320	## Test coverage
321	
322	`tests/services/issue-service.test.ts` exercises the full public surface: creation quota
323	enforcement, status transition idempotence, assignment branching (assign vs. unassign),
324	archive-then-mutate rejections, and the `getIssue`/`listIssues`/`getBoard` read paths.
325	`tests/services/issue-service.scope.test.ts` is a narrower, dedicated suite that runs every
326	mutating function against the same table of cross-tenant and under-permissioned actors,
327	confirming the guard order documented in DES-100 fails on tenant scope before it fails on
328	permission, and on permission before it reveals archived state. No other test file in the
329	corpus exercises this service directly, though `tests/jobs/digest-email-job.test.ts` and
330	`tests/services/notification-service.test.ts` cover downstream consumers of the events this
331	service emits.

status: approved
owners: [m.lindqvist]
last_updated: 2026-05-22

## Purpose

`src/server/services/issue-service.ts` owns everything that turns a create/update/status
request into a row in the `issues` table plus the events every reactive concern in Taskflow
hangs off: notifications (DES-121 .. DES-127), search indexing (DES-154 .. DES-158), the
audit log (DES-170 .. DES-174), webhook fan-out (DES-159 .. DES-163) and the usage counters
(DES-135 .. DES-141). It is the largest service in the layer by function count because an
issue is the object almost everything else in the product reacts to.

What it deliberately does not own: numbering scheme storage (delegated to
`src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts`'s `nextIssueNumber`), label assignment (owned
by `src/server/services/label-service.ts`), attachment quota accounting (owned by
`src/server/services/attachment-service.ts`), and comment threading (owned by
`src/server/services/comment-service.ts`). Board rendering order is explicitly
presentation-only — DES-104 covers why `moveIssue` does not persist a position column.

Every exported function follows the same shape and it is worth stating once instead of
per-function: `assertOrgScope` first, then a `requireFound` load of the row (or its parent,
for `createIssue`), then `assertCan` against a `PermissionResource` built by one of the
`_support.ts` helpers, then `assertNotArchived` where archiving matters, then the write, then
`emit`. DES-100 names this order explicitly because two tests
(`tests/services/issue-service.test.ts`, `tests/services/issue-service.scope.test.ts`) assert
on it directly by checking which error surfaces when two guards would both fail.

## Public surface

| function | signature | permission action | events emitted | errors thrown |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `createIssue` | `(actor: Actor, input: CreateIssueInput) => Promise<Issue>` | `issue:create` | `issue.created` | `NotFoundError`, `PermissionDeniedError`, `AlreadyArchivedError`, plain `Error` (quota) |
| `updateIssue` | `(actor: Actor, input: UpdateIssueInput) => Promise<Issue>` | `issue:update` | `issue.updated` | `NotFoundError`, `PermissionDeniedError`, `AlreadyArchivedError` |
| `changeIssueStatus` | `(actor: Actor, input: ChangeIssueStatusInput) => Promise<Issue>` | `issue:update` | `issue.status_changed` | `NotFoundError`, `PermissionDeniedError`, `AlreadyArchivedError` |
| `assignIssue` | `(actor: Actor, input: AssignIssueInput) => Promise<Issue>` | `issue:assign` | `issue.assigned` or `issue.updated` | `NotFoundError`, `PermissionDeniedError`, `AlreadyArchivedError` |
| `archiveIssue` | `(actor: Actor, orgId: OrgId, issueId: IssueId) => Promise<Issue>` | `issue:archive` | `issue.archived` | `NotFoundError`, `PermissionDeniedError`, `AlreadyArchivedError` |
| `moveIssue` | `(actor: Actor, input: MoveIssueInput) => Promise<Issue>` | `issue:update` (delegated) | `issue.status_changed` | same as `changeIssueStatus` |
| `getIssue` | `(actor: Actor, orgId: OrgId, issueId: IssueId) => Promise<IssueWithRelations>` | `issue:read` | none | `NotFoundError`, `PermissionDeniedError` |
| `listIssues` | `(actor: Actor, input: IssueFilterInput) => Promise<Page<Issue>>` | `issue:read` | none | `PermissionDeniedError` |
| `getBoard` | `(actor: Actor, orgId: OrgId, projectId: ProjectId) => Promise<readonly IssueBoardColumn[]>` | `issue:read` | none | `NotFoundError`, `PermissionDeniedError` |

the permission surface for a distinction the product has never asked for.

### DES-104 — Board drag-and-drop is a status change plus a touch, not a persisted order

- **Satisfies:** REQ-066, REQ-077
- **Decided in:** ADR-021
- **Code:** `src/server/services/issue-service.ts` — `moveIssue`, `getBoard`

`moveIssue` is a thin wrapper: it takes a `MoveIssueInput` (`orgId`, `issueId`, `toStatus`)
and calls `changeIssueStatus(actor, { orgId, issueId, status: input.toStatus })` directly,
inheriting every guard and event from DES-103 rather than duplicating them. The code comment
in the source is explicit about why there is no persisted card index: "the index is
presentation-only — the board renders by `updated_at`." That means two clients dragging cards
in the same column concurrently do not fight over an integer position column; the board's
sort order is a side effect of `changeIssueStatus`'s write, which always touches `updated_at`.
The trade-off is that a user who drags a card to a different position *within* the same
status column, without changing status, produces no repository write and no visible reorder
after a refresh — the UI only persists cross-column moves. `getBoard` is a pure read: it loads
the project, asserts `issue:read` against it, and defers entirely to
`issueRepo.listBoardColumns`, which does the status-bucketing server-side so the client never
computes columns from a flat issue list.

### DES-105 — Assignment is a separate permission from update, and un-assigning degrades to issue.updated

- **Satisfies:** REQ-067
- **Decided in:** ADR-003, ADR-005
- **Code:** `src/server/services/issue-service.ts` — `assignIssue`

`assignIssue` checks `issue:assign`, a permission distinct from `issue:update` in
`ROLE_MATRIX` (both require `member` minimum, but they are separate matrix entries so a
future role split does not have to touch this call site). The reason assignment has its own
permission at all, per the source comment, is that a member may need to reassign work they do
not otherwise own — reassigning a stuck issue away from an absent teammate is a common
workflow that should not require `issue:update` rights over content the reassigner did not
author. The function branches on `input.assigneeId === null`: unassigning publishes
`issue.updated` with `changedFields: ["assigneeId"]` rather than `issue.assigned`, because
`issue.assigned`'s payload contract requires a non-null `assigneeId` — `TaskflowEventMap`
types the field as `UserId`, not `UserId | null`, so a null assignment literally cannot be
represented in that event shape. Assigning to a real user publishes `issue.assigned` carrying
both `previousAssigneeId: before.assigneeId` and the new `assigneeId`, which is what lets
`notification-service.ts`'s `issue.assigned` handler notify only the new assignee (DES-122)
without a second lookup, and what lets the activity log render "Assigned to X" without
needing the prior value.

### DES-106 — getIssue composes three repositories into one read model, and never authorizes the composed pieces separately

- **Satisfies:** REQ-074, REQ-075, REQ-077
- **Decided in:** ADR-013
- **Code:** `src/server/services/issue-service.ts` — `getIssue`

`getIssue` authorizes once, against `issue:read` on the loaded issue, and then freely composes
three additional repository reads without further permission checks: `labelRepo
.listLabelsForIssues` (REQ-074, org-shared labels), `commentRepo.countComments`, and
`attachmentRepo.listAttachments(...).length` (REQ-075, storage-quota-tracked attachments).
This is a deliberate reading of ADR-013's "services own authorization, repositories own
tenancy" boundary: once a caller has proven they may read the issue, its label assignments,
comment count, and attachment count are treated as part of the same resource rather than as
independently protected sub-resources, because none of them can be read meaningfully on their
own — a label list without knowing which issue it decorates, or a comment count without the
issue it counts, has no product surface. This is narrower than `comment-service.ts`'s
`getThread`, which re-checks `comment:read` even though it also starts from a loaded issue —
the two services made different calls about whether the sub-resource has its own reachable
endpoint (comments do, via `/issues/:id/comments`; label and attachment *counts* on the issue
detail view do not).

### DES-107 — listIssues authorizes at the organization, not per project, because visibility narrows later

- **Satisfies:** REQ-050, REQ-077, REQ-078
- **Decided in:** ADR-008
- **Code:** `src/server/services/issue-service.ts` — `listIssues`

`listIssues` asserts `issue:read` against `orgResource(input.orgId)` rather than against any
individual project, with an explicit comment marking the trade-off: "a cross-project list is
an org-wide read; per-project visibility is enforced when the caller opens an individual
issue." That means a viewer with org-wide `issue:read` can see issue titles and statuses from
a project whose visibility is `private` in the same paginated list, and only hits a
permission wall if they try to open one. The team accepted this because private projects
(REQ-050) gate discovery, not existence — the alternative, filtering the list per-project
before pagination, would require joining project visibility into every keyset page (ADR-008)
and would make `IssueFilterInput`'s cursor semantics depend on membership state that can
change between pages. `listIssues` otherwise does no work of its own: filtering by status,
assignee and label is delegated entirely to `issueRepo.listIssues(input)`, which implements
REQ-077's filter surface and REQ-078's keyset pagination.

## Sequence: creating an issue and its downstream fan-out

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant UI as Issue create form
    participant Action as Server Action
    participant Svc as issue-service.createIssue
    participant Repo as issue-repository
    participant Bus as event-bus.emit
    participant Notif as notification-service
    participant Search as search-service
    participant Activity as activity-service

    UI->>Action: submit CreateIssueInput
    Action->>Svc: createIssue(actor, input)
    Svc->>Svc: assertOrgScope(actor, input.orgId)
    Svc->>Repo: findProjectById
    Repo-->>Svc: project
    Svc->>Svc: assertNotArchived(project)
    Svc->>Svc: assertCan(issue:create, projectResource)
    Svc->>Repo: countIssues(orgId, projectId)
    Repo-->>Svc: used
    Svc->>Svc: wouldExceedLimit(plan, "issuesPerProject", used)
    Svc->>Repo: nextIssueNumber
    Repo-->>Svc: number
    Svc->>Repo: insertIssue
    Repo-->>Svc: issue
    Svc->>Bus: emit("issue.created", payload)
    Bus-->>Notif: (no direct subscriber to issue.created)
    Bus-->>Search: subscribe handler re-reads row, indexIssue
    Bus-->>Activity: subscribe handler records activity row
    Svc-->>Action: issue
    Action-->>UI: issue
```

1. The UI submits a validated `CreateIssueInput` to a Server Action, which forwards it
   unchanged to `createIssue(actor, input)`.
2. The service asserts tenant scope first, then loads the parent project and confirms it is
   not archived before checking `issue:create` against it — a caller who cannot even see the
   project never learns whether the quota has room.
3. `issueRepo.countIssues` returns the current count for the quota comparison; `createIssue`
   never inserts the row before this check succeeds.
4. `issueRepo.nextIssueNumber` is only called once every prior gate has passed, so a rejected
   request leaves no gap in the per-project numbering sequence.
5. `issueRepo.insertIssue` writes the row and returns the persisted `Issue`, including its
   generated id and number.
6. `emit("issue.created", ...)` publishes the event synchronously to every subscriber
   registered through `event-registry.ts`; note that, unlike `issue.assigned`, no
   notification handler subscribes to `issue.created` directly — issue creation notifies
   nobody by design, since there is no assignee or mentioned user yet.
7. The search listener (DES-158) re-reads the issue by id rather than trusting the payload
   and calls `indexIssue`; the activity listener (DES-172) writes an audit row from the
   payload directly, since activity intentionally trusts event payloads for its summary text.
8. Control returns to the Server Action once `emit` resolves — Taskflow's event bus is
   in-process and awaited, so a slow subscriber delays the response; this is the accepted
   trade-off ADR-005 documents in exchange for never losing an event to a queue outage.

## Failure modes

| thrown error | resulting error code | caller behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `NotFoundError` (from `requireFound`) | `not_found` (404) | UI shows "issue/project not found"; Server Action surfaces a toast, no retry |
| `PermissionDeniedError` (from `assertCan`) | `forbidden` (403) | Server Action returns a form error; UI hides the action that produced it once role is known |
| `TenantScopeError` (from `assertOrgScope`) | `tenant_scope_violation` (403) | Treated as a programming error client-side; logged, session redirected to org switcher |
| `AlreadyArchivedError` (from `assertNotArchived`) | `conflict` (409) | UI prompts to restore the project/issue before retrying the write |
| plain `Error` (quota message in `createIssue`) | falls through to `internal_error` (500) unless mapped upstream | UI shows a generic failure; this is a known gap — quota breaches in `issue-service.ts` are not raised as a typed `plan_limit_exceeded` the way `billing-service.ts`'s `assertWithinLimit` does, so the client cannot distinguish a quota breach from a genuine server fault by error code alone |

The quota-error inconsistency in the last row is real and worth flagging in review: unlike
`project-service.ts`'s `createProject` (same pattern) and `billing-service.ts`'s
`assertWithinLimit` (which emits `billing.limit_exceeded` and is designed to map to
`plan_limit_exceeded`), `createIssue` throws a bare `Error` with a human-readable message
rather than a typed domain error. `src/lib/errors.ts`'s `HTTP_STATUS_BY_CODE` has no entry a
bare `Error` maps to other than the `internal_error` default, so a caller cannot render a
"upgrade your plan" call to action from the error alone today; the UI currently pattern
matches on the message string, which is fragile and flagged as a follow-up in the DES-135
billing design.

## Test coverage

`tests/services/issue-service.test.ts` exercises the full public surface: creation quota
enforcement, status transition idempotence, assignment branching (assign vs. unassign),
archive-then-mutate rejections, and the `getIssue`/`listIssues`/`getBoard` read paths.
`tests/services/issue-service.scope.test.ts` is a narrower, dedicated suite that runs every
mutating function against the same table of cross-tenant and under-permissioned actors,
confirming the guard order documented in DES-100 fails on tenant scope before it fails on
permission, and on permission before it reveals archived state. No other test file in the
corpus exercises this service directly, though `tests/jobs/digest-email-job.test.ts` and
`tests/services/notification-service.test.ts` cover downstream consumers of the events this
service emits.

10	## Scope
11	
12	This document defines the requirements for issues: numbering, the status and priority
13	vocabularies, creation quota, the events issue mutations emit, due dates and overdue
14	detection, archiving, cross-project moves, listing and filtering, attachments, and CSV
15	export. It is the largest single domain in the requirements corpus because issues are the
16	object most of the rest of the product orbits — comments, notifications, search and activity
17	all key off issue events defined here.
18	
19	## Context
20	
21	`src/server/services/issue-service.ts` is the sole owner of issue business rules; every
22	mutation goes through it, with one deliberate exception the brief calls out explicitly: the
23	issue detail page at
24	`src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/projects/[projectSlug]/issues/[issueNumber]/page.tsx` reads
25	directly from `issue-repository.ts` for its initial render rather than through the service,
26	a known layering exception kept for a fast first paint on the single highest-traffic page in
27	the app. Every mutation, by contrast, always goes through `issue-service.ts`, which composes
28	`assertCan()`, `assertOrgScope()`, `wouldExceedLimit()` and `assertNotArchived()` before
29	touching the repository.
30	
31	Issue identity has two parts: a database `IssueId` (a branded ULID, `ADR-015`) and a
32	human-facing number that is unique only within its project, allocated by
33	`issue-repository.ts#nextIssueNumber` and never reused (`REQ-061`) — even after an issue is
34	archived or, in principle, deleted, its number is retired, so `ENG-142` always means the
35	same issue for the life of the project. `issueKey(projectKey, issueNumber)` in
36	`src/lib/format.ts` is what renders the two together as the identifier users actually see
37	and type.
38	
39	Status and priority are closed vocabularies (`REQ-062`, `REQ-063`) defined in
40	`src/types/issue.ts` and mirrored in `src/schemas/issue.ts` for runtime validation — there
41	is no admin UI to add a fifth status, unlike labels, which are free-form per organization.
42	Every status transition and every assignment change emits its own event
43	(`issue.status_changed`, `issue.assigned`) distinct from the general `issue.updated`, which
44	itself only reports the fields that actually changed (`REQ-068`) rather than the whole
45	record, keeping downstream consumers — notifications, search reindexing, activity — from
46	doing needless work or producing noisy "issue updated" rows for a field nobody watches.
47	
48	Overdue detection is not computed on read; `overdue-issue-job.ts` sweeps on a schedule
49	(`REQ-070`) and emits `issue.overdue`, because computing "is this overdue" per page view
50	across every list and board would mean every issue list query also needs `now()`-relative
51	logic duplicated across the board view, the list view and the notification fan-out, instead
52	of one job producing one event the rest of the system reacts to uniformly.

55	
56	1. `REQ-076`'s renumbering on cross-project move means an issue's number is not stable

58	   pair should redirect rather than 404 is unresolved.
59	2. `REQ-075` counts attachments against `storageMb`, but there is no requirement here for
60	   what happens to that count when an issue carrying attachments is permanently purged by
61	   the retention job (`REQ-231`) — see the corresponding gap noted in
62	   `billing-and-plan-limits.md`.
63	3. `REQ-079`'s CSV export flag-gates on plan, but does not additionally rate-limit large
64	   exports; a very large `issuesPerProject` on `enterprise` combined with unlimited export
65	   frequency is a known cost surface, not yet bounded by a requirement.

67	### REQ-060 — An issue belongs to exactly one project

69	- **Priority:** must
70	- **Status:** implemented
71	- **Related:** REQ-040, REQ-010, DES-070
72	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts` — `findIssueById`, `insertIssue`
73	- **Verified by:** `tests/repositories/issue-repository.test.ts`
74	
75	`issues` carries both `org_id` and `project_id`; every `issue-repository.ts` function takes
76	`orgId` first, and most also take or resolve a `projectId`. There is no cross-project issue
77	and no "backlog" issue unattached to a project — creating an issue always requires choosing

80	**Acceptance criteria**
81	
82	1. `createIssue` requires a valid, non-archived `projectId` within the actor's org.
83	2. `findIssueById` scoped to the wrong `projectId` for that issue returns `null`, not the
84	   issue from a different project.

88	
89	- **Priority:** must
90	- **Status:** implemented
91	- **Related:** DES-070, ADR-008, REQ-042
92

94	project; `insertIssue` is given that number explicitly rather than deriving it itself, so the
95	allocation and the insert are two distinct, testable steps. Numbers are never recycled: an
96	archived or moved-away issue's old number stays retired, because `ENG-142` having meant two
97	different things at different points in the project's history would break every saved link,
98	comment permalink and search result referencing it.
99	
100	**Acceptance criteria**
101	
102	1. `nextIssueNumber` never returns a value already used by a live or archived issue in that
103	   project.
104	2. Two concurrent `createIssue` calls for the same project never receive the same number.
105	3. Deleting the highest-numbered issue in a project does not cause the next created issue to
106	   reuse that number.
107	
108	**Implemented by:** `src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts` — `nextIssueNumber`, `insertIssue`
109	**Verified by:** `tests/repositories/issue-repository.test.ts`

113	- **Priority:** must
114	- **Status:** implemented
115	- **Related:** REQ-066, REQ-077, DES-071
116	- **Implemented by:** `src/types/issue.ts`, `src/schemas/issue.ts`, `src/lib/format.ts` — `humanizeStatus`
117	- **Verified by:** `tests/schemas/issue.schema.test.ts`, `tests/lib/format.test.ts`

137	- **Status:** implemented

144	`humanizePriority`. Unlike status, priority has no transition rules of its own — any

161	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/issue-service.ts` — `createIssue`, `src/config/plan-limits.ts` — `wouldExceedLimit`

202	
203	- **Priority:** must
204	- **Status:** implemented
205	- **Related:** REQ-062, REQ-111, DES-070
206	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/issue-service.ts` — `changeIssueStatus`
207	- **Verified by:** `tests/services/issue-service.test.ts`
208	
209	`changeIssueStatus` emits `issue.status_changed`, distinct from the general `issue.updated`
210	event a plain field edit would emit, because status transitions are the event most
211	notification preferences and most activity-feed filters specifically care about — a
212	recipient who mutes general issue-update notifications may still want status-change alerts,
213	which the two-event split makes possible without payload-level filtering.
214	
215	**Acceptance criteria**
216	
217	1. `issue.status_changed`'s payload includes both the previous and new status.
218	2. Calling `updateIssue` with an unchanged status does not additionally emit
219	   `issue.status_changed`; only `changeIssueStatus` emits it.
220	3. A no-op status "change" (new status equals current status) either short-circuits before
221	   emitting or is rejected by validation, not silently emitted as a real transition.
222	
223	### REQ-067 — Assignment emits issue.assigned with the previous assignee
224	
225	- **Priority:** must
226	- **Status:** implemented
227	- **Related:** REQ-113, REQ-068
228	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/issue-service.ts` — `assignIssue`
229	- **Verified by:** `tests/services/issue-service.test.ts`
230	
231	`assignIssue` emits `issue.assigned` carrying both the new assignee and the previous one
232	(which may be `null`), which is what lets the notification service decide whether to notify
233	the newly assigned person and, separately, whether the previous assignee needs to know they
234	were unassigned — two different notification semantics from one event.
235	
236	**Acceptance criteria**
237	
238	1. Unassigning an issue (setting assignee to `null`) still emits `issue.assigned` with the
239	   new value `null` and the prior assignee populated.
240	2. `issue.assigned`'s `actorId` is the person making the change, not the new assignee,
241	   unless they are the same person.
242	3. Self-assignment still emits the event; there is no special-cased suppression for
243	   assigning to oneself.
244	
245	### REQ-068 — Only the changed fields are reported on issue.updated
246	
247	- **Priority:** should
248	- **Status:** implemented
249	- **Related:** REQ-066, REQ-067, DES-071
250	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/issue-service.ts` — `updateIssue`
251	- **Verified by:** `tests/services/issue-service.test.ts`
252	
253	`updateIssue` diffs the incoming patch against the current row and includes only the fields
254	that actually changed in the `issue.updated` payload, rather than the full before/after
255	issue. This keeps activity-feed summaries specific ("changed description") instead of
256	generic ("issue updated"), and avoids the payload bloat of shipping an entire issue record
257	on every minor edit.
258	
259	**Acceptance criteria**
260	
261	1. Updating only the `description` field produces an `issue.updated` payload naming
262	   `description` and no other field.
263	2. A no-op update (patch identical to current values) either emits no event or an
264	   empty-changed-fields event that downstream consumers treat as a no-op; it must not appear
265	   as a substantive change in the activity feed.
266	3. Status and assignee changes routed through their dedicated events (`REQ-066`, `REQ-067`)
267	   are not also duplicated in `issue.updated`'s changed-field list when they arrive via
268	   `changeIssueStatus`/`assignIssue` rather than `updateIssue`.
269	
270	### REQ-069 — Issues may carry a due date
271	
272	- **Priority:** should
273	- **Status:** implemented
274	- **Related:** REQ-070, REQ-012
275	- **Implemented by:** `src/schemas/issue.ts`, `src/lib/date.ts` — `isOverdue`
276	- **Verified by:** `tests/schemas/issue.schema.test.ts`, `tests/lib/date.test.ts`
277	
278	`dueAt` is a nullable `IsoTimestamp` field on the issue, settable through `createIssue` or
279	`updateIssue`. It is the input `isOverdue()` in `src/lib/date.ts` and the overdue sweep job
280	both key off; an issue with no due date is by definition never overdue.
281	
282	**Acceptance criteria**
283	
284	1. `dueAt` is optional on creation and clearable (settable back to `null`) on update.
285	2. `dueAt` accepts any valid `IsoTimestamp`, past or future — Taskflow does not reject a due
286	   date in the past at write time, since backfilling overdue work is a legitimate use.
287	3. Clearing `dueAt` on an issue already flagged overdue removes it from future overdue
288	   sweeps.
289	
290	### REQ-070 — Overdue issues are detected by a scheduled sweep
291	
292	- **Priority:** should
293	- **Status:** implemented
294	- **Related:** REQ-069, REQ-111, ADR-016
295	
296	`runOverdueIssueJob(now)` in `src/server/jobs/overdue-issue-job.ts` calls
297	`listOverdueIssues(orgId, now)` per organization and emits `issue.overdue` for each newly
298	overdue issue, on the `overdue-issues` cadence (every 60 minutes per `CADENCE_MINUTES`).
299	Overdue status is not stored as a persistent flag on the issue row; it is a derived
300	computation the job repeats each tick, filtered through `shouldFilterArchived` so an archived
301	issue past its due date is never reported overdue.
302	
303	**Acceptance criteria**
304	
305	1. The job only considers non-archived issues with a non-null `dueAt` in the past relative
306	   to `now`.
307	2. Re-running the job within the same hour does not emit a duplicate `issue.overdue` for an
308	   issue already reported overdue in a prior tick within the same cadence window.
309	3. Archiving an issue removes it from subsequent overdue sweeps immediately.
310	
311	**Implemented by:** `src/server/jobs/overdue-issue-job.ts`
312	**Verified by:** `tests/jobs/overdue-issue-job.test.ts`
313	
314	### REQ-071 — Issues are archived, not deleted, by default
315	
316	- **Priority:** must
317	- **Status:** implemented
318	- **Related:** ADR-004, REQ-046, REQ-073
319	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/issue-service.ts` — `archiveIssue`, `src/lib/soft-delete.ts` — `shouldFilterArchived`
320	- **Verified by:** `tests/services/issue-service.test.ts`, `tests/lib/soft-delete.test.ts`
321	
322	`archiveIssue` sets `archived_at` via `archivePatch()`; there is no `deleteIssue` in

324	`shouldFilterArchived` is applied by default across `listIssues`, `listBoardColumns` and
325	`countIssues`, so archived issues vanish from active work views while remaining fully
326	queryable with an explicit scope.
327	
328	**Acceptance criteria**
329	
330	1. `archiveIssue` never issues a `DELETE` statement.
331	2. `listIssues` without an explicit scope excludes archived issues.
332	3. `AlreadyArchivedError` is thrown, not silently ignored, when archiving an already-archived
333	   issue twice.
334	
335	### REQ-072 — Authors and assignees may edit an issue they do not otherwise own
336	
337	- **Priority:** must
338	- **Status:** implemented
339	- **Related:** REQ-026, ADR-003
340	- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/permissions.ts` — `can`
341	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/permissions.ownership.test.ts`
342	
343	This is the issue-specific instance of the ownership-escalation rule defined generally in
344	`REQ-026`: `issue:update` and `issue:archive` are granted to the issue's author or its
345	current assignee even when their role rank alone would not clear the matrix minimum. It
346	means a `member` newly demoted to a role that could no longer create new issues still
347	retains control over issues already assigned to or authored by them, until an `admin`
348	explicitly reassigns that work.
349	
350	**Acceptance criteria**
351	
352	1. `can(actor, 'issue:update', issue)` is `true` when `actor.userId` equals `issue.authorId`
353	   or `issue.assigneeId`, regardless of role.
354	2. The same escalation applies to `issue:archive`.
355	3. Escalation does not extend to `issue:delete`, which stays admin-only (`REQ-073`)
356	   irrespective of authorship.
357	
358	### REQ-073 — Issue deletion requires admin
359	
360	- **Priority:** should
361	- **Status:** implemented
362	- **Related:** REQ-024, REQ-072
363	- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/permissions.ts` — `ROLE_MATRIX`
364	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts`
365	
366	`issue:delete`'s `ROLE_MATRIX` minimum is `admin`, one of the few issue actions ownership
367	escalation does not reach (`REQ-072`). As with projects and organizations, there is no
368	interactive hard-delete Server Action for issues today — permanent removal only happens
369	through the retention cleanup job once an archived issue passes the plan's retention window.
370	
371	**Acceptance criteria**
372	
373	1. A `member` who authored an issue still cannot permanently delete it, only archive it.
374	2. `issue:delete`'s matrix entry exists and is exercised by
375	   `tests/lib/permissions.matrix.test.ts` even though no current action exposes it directly.
376	3. The only code path that removes an issue row entirely is the retention cleanup job.
377	
378	### REQ-074 — Issues carry organization labels
379	
380	- **Priority:** should
381	- **Status:** implemented
382	- **Related:** REQ-013, DES-100
383	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/repositories/label-repository.ts` — `setIssueLabels`, `listLabelsForIssues`
384	- **Verified by:** none — covered indirectly; see the gaps section of the test plan
385	
386	`setIssueLabels(orgId, issueId, labelIds)` attaches labels from the organization-wide label
387	set (`REQ-013`) to an issue; `listLabelsForIssues` batches the reverse lookup for list and
388	board views so rendering a page of issues does not issue one label query per row.
389	
390	**Acceptance criteria**
391	
392	1. A label id from a different organization cannot be attached to an issue (enforced by the
393	   `orgId`-scoped label lookup before `setIssueLabels` writes the join rows).
394	2. `listLabelsForIssues` returns a map keyed by issue id, even for issues with zero labels
395	   (an empty array, not a missing key).
396	3. Deleting a label detaches it from every issue that referenced it (see `REQ-013`).
397	
398	### REQ-075 — Issue attachments are counted against the storage quota
399	
400	- **Priority:** should
401	- **Status:** implemented

403	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/attachment-service.ts` — `addAttachment`, `src/server/repositories/attachment-repository.ts` — `sumStorageBytes`
404	- **Verified by:** none — covered indirectly; see the gaps section of the test plan
405	
406	`attachment-service.ts#addAttachment` calls `wouldExceedLimit(plan, 'storageMb', used)`
407	before `attachment-repository.ts#insertAttachment` runs, where `used` comes from
408	`sumStorageBytes(orgId)` converted to megabytes. Attachments are metadata rows in this
409	codebase — actual byte storage is out of scope for the corpus's fictional backend — but the
410	size accounting they carry is real and is what the quota check reads.
411	
412	**Acceptance criteria**
413	
414	1. Adding an attachment that would push `storageMb` over the plan's limit fails with
415	   `plan_limit_exceeded`.
416	2. `sumStorageBytes` reflects only attachments belonging to the requesting org.
417	3. Removing an attachment (`removeAttachment`) frees the storage it held for subsequent
418	   quota checks.
419	
420	### REQ-076 — Moving an issue between projects renumbers it
421	
422	- **Priority:** should
423	- **Status:** implemented
424	- **Related:** REQ-061, REQ-042
425	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/issue-service.ts` — `moveIssue`
426	- **Verified by:** `tests/services/issue-service.test.ts`

429	number there, since issue numbers are scoped per project (`REQ-061`) and a number from the
430	source project could already be taken in the destination. The issue keeps its identity
431	(`IssueId`) and history; only its display number and `issueKey` prefix change.
432	
433	**Acceptance criteria**
434	
435	1. After `moveIssue`, the issue's number is unique within the destination project.
436	2. The issue's old number is not reassigned to a new issue in the source project
437	   afterward, consistent with `REQ-061`'s never-reused guarantee.
438	3. `moveIssue` emits `issue.updated` reporting the `projectId` change, so search and
439	   activity stay consistent with the new location.
440	
441	### REQ-077 — Issue listings support filtering by status, assignee and label
442	
443	- **Priority:** must
444	- **Status:** implemented
445	- **Related:** REQ-062, REQ-074, DES-100
446	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts` — `listIssues`, `listIssuesWithRelations`
447	- **Verified by:** `tests/repositories/issue-repository.test.ts`, `tests/components/issue-filter-params.test.ts`
448	
449	`IssueFilterInput` accepts status, assignee and label filters, consumed by
450	`listIssues`/`listIssuesWithRelations`. These three are the filters the board view and the
451	list view both build their query-string state around, since they are the axes teams actually
452	triage by day to day.
453	
454	**Acceptance criteria**
455	
456	1. Combining status, assignee and label filters in one call applies them conjunctively
457	   (AND), not disjunctively.
458	2. An empty filter set returns the same result as `listIssues` with no filter object.
459	3. Filtering by a label id from another org returns an empty page rather than erroring.
460	
461	### REQ-078 — Issue listings are paginated by keyset cursor
462	
463	- **Priority:** must
464	- **Status:** implemented
465	- **Related:** REQ-052, ADR-008
466	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts` — `listIssues`, `src/server/repositories/base-repository.ts` — `encodeCursor`, `decodeCursor`
467	- **Verified by:** `tests/repositories/issue-repository.test.ts`

474	**Acceptance criteria**
475	
476	1. `listIssues`'s cursor round-trips through `encodeCursor`/`decodeCursor` without loss.
477	2. A filtered listing (`REQ-077`) paginates correctly — the cursor encodes position within

480	   of what the caller asks for.

483	
484	- **Priority:** could
485	- **Status:** implemented
486	- **Related:** REQ-230, ADR-010, DES-110
487	- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/csv.ts` — `toCsv`, `src/app/api/export/issues/route.ts`
488	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/csv.test.ts`
489

498	   `feature_disabled`-shaped `AppErrorShape`, when attempting export.
499	2. Exported CSV columns match the fields visible in the corresponding list view.
500	3. `toCsv` output round-trips through `escapeCsvValue` for any title or description
501	   containing a comma, quote or newline (`REQ-230`).
